title: Localization functor Loc_φ: Rep(G) → Cosh_G(X, R, φ)
body_html:
Localization functor $\mathrm{Loc}_\phi$

Let $\Cosh_G(X, R, \phi)$ be the full subcategory of $\Cosh_G(X, R)$ on those $\mathscr{V}$ such that $K_E$ acts on $\mathscr{V}_E$ via $\phi_E$: i.e.\ $\mathscr{V} = \mathscr{V}[\phi]$ where $\mathscr{V}[\phi]E := (\mathscr{V}_E|{K_E})[\phi_E]$. By Invariants and coinvariants of G-equivariant (co)sheaves, $\mathscr{V}[\phi]$ is itself an object of $\Cosh_G(X, R)$.

Definition. The localization functor $$\Loc_\phi : \Rep(G) \to \Cosh_G(X, R, \phi)$$ is defined on stalks by $$\Loc_\phi(V)_E \;:=\; (V|_{K_E})[\phi_E].$$

The restriction maps $r^{\Loc_\phi(V)}_{E,E'}$ are induced from the compatibility $\phi_E|_{K_{E'}} = \phi_{E'}$ for $E \preceq E'$ (the sheaf direction); the $G$-action is the restriction of the $G$-action on $V$.

For $V \in \Rep_\phi(G)$, the restricted functor $\Loc_\phi : \Rep_\phi(G) \to \Cosh_G(X, R, \phi)$ has a left adjoint built from chain homology, namely [[node:representations.h0_C_dot_adjoint]].
